summary: Nikolai Solmsdorf is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Munich under doctoral supervisor Franz-Karl Ehrhard, also studying under Alexander von Rospatt, and held a post at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Nikolai Trubetzkoy (1890–1938) was a linguist who studied at Moscow University (~1908–1913) and under August Leskien (~1913–1914). He held posts at Sofia University (~1920–1922) and the University of Vienna (~1922–1938).
Nima Repper is an Indologist who served as a Wissenschaftliche Mitarbeiterin and studied at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Nina Mirnig is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who founded the Indology Graduate Seminar in 2008. She held positions at the University of Groningen, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia, and the University of Vienna.

Ninian Smart (1927–2001) was a religious studies and philosophy scholar educated at Glasgow, Oxford, and Yale. He held professorships at the University of Birmingham (1961), Lancaster University (1967–1982), and the University of California, Santa Barbara (1976–1998).

Nira Wickramasinghe (born 1964) is a historian and Indologist. She studied at the University of Paris (~1981–1985) and the University of Oxford (~1985–1989), and was appointed Professor of Modern South Asian Studies at Leiden University (~2010).

Nirajan Kafle is an Indologist who completed his doctorate at Leiden University under Peter C. Bisschop (to 2015). He worked at the Nepal Research Centre (2008–2015), the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (2019), and Leiden University (2021).
Niran Rajvamshi is a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. In 2018, he held posts at the National Archives of Nepal and on the editorial board of Documenta Nepalica.

Niranjan Prasad Chakravarti (1893–1956) was an Indologist and historian who studied at Calcutta, Cambridge, Paris, and Berlin. He taught at Calcutta (1917) and held various posts at the Archaeological Survey of India, serving as Director General from 1948 to 1950.

Nirbhay N. Singh is a scholar in religious studies and related fields. He has served as Professor at Virginia Commonwealth University, Director at the Commonwealth Institute for Family Studies, and Clinical Professor of Psychiatry and Health Behavior at Augusta University.
Nirmal C. Sinha served as the editor of the Bulletin of Tibetology, attested in 1978 and 1988.

Nirmal Chandra Sinha (1911–1997) was a scholar in Tibetology and history who studied at Presidency University and Calcutta University. He was the founder director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (1958–1987) and Centenary Professor at Calcutta University (1971).
Nirupam Chakma is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing (attested 2015).
Noa Gal is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies who completed a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Oxford under the supervision of Richard Gombrich (attested 2003).

Noa Ronkin is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. She completed a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich (to 2003) and served as a Lecturer and Research Fellow at Stanford University (attested 2005).

Noboru Karashima (1933–2015) was a historian and Indologist who earned his degrees at the University of Tokyo. He held multiple academic posts at the University of Tokyo (1964–1994) and served as a professor at Taisho University (~1994–2008).

Noboru Miyata (1936–2000) was a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and history. He studied at Tokyo University of Education and the University of Tsukuba, later serving as Professor of Folklore at Tsukuba (~1979–1999) and at Kanagawa University (~1999–2000).
Noboru Ueda is a scholar in Buddhist studies who held a post at the University of Tokyo (attested 1990) and served as a professor at Mejiro University (attested 2015).

Nobuchiyo Kotani (born 1944) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Otani University and Kyoto University (under Yuichi Kajiyama) and served as Professor at Otani University (~1985–2014) and President of Otani University Junior College (~1999–2007).

Nobuhiko Kobayashi is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University. He has held positions at the University of Toronto (attested 1969), Kyoto University (attested 1979), and Taisho University (attested 2026).
